summary: Apply FAO food security dimensions, SAFA, and climate-risk concepts to food-system decisions. Explore the five-day course and plan your learning.
lede: Food-system sustainability planning weighs climate and resource pressures alongside food availability, access, and stability. For food-policy officers, agriculture programme planners, and supply-chain sustainability specialists, the course develops practical skills in mapping climate risks, comparing production options, and appraising interventions. Participants use the FAO food security dimensions, SAFA, and SDG 2 to shape an action plan and select indicators for decision-making and progress reporting.
audienceIntro: This foundation course suits professionals who connect food access and production choices with environmental pressures, programme design, or food-system investment.
modules: FAO Food Security Dimensions and SDG 2
IPCC Climate Risk in Food Systems
prerequisites: No prior food-security or sustainability qualification is required. Familiarity with food, agriculture, or programme work is useful. No coding or programming is required.
